h1: Probate & Small Estate Affidavits Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: After a death in the family, someone has to get the house, the vehicles and the bank accounts into the right names. Attorney Robert Navar helps El Paso families pick the simplest Texas probate path that works and handles the filing in the El Paso County probate courts.
summary: A small estate affidavit (Estates Code Ch. 205) can transfer assets without a full probate when there is no will, the estate is worth $75,000 or less excluding the homestead and exempt property, and at least 30 days have passed since death.
A muniment of title (Ch. 257) admits a valid will to probate as a title document — no executor appointed — when the estate owes no debts other than those secured by real estate.

Independent administration (Ch. 401) is the standard full probate: the court appoints an executor or administrator who acts with minimal court supervision. Texas courts generally require that the representative be represented by an attorney.

El Paso County probate matters are filed at the County Courthouse, 500 E. San Antonio Ave. We quote a flat fee after a free consultation for most uncontested matters. Schedule an appointment or call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: Which Probate Path Fits Your Family's Situation
paragraphs: Texas probate is less a single process than a choice of tools. The questions that decide it are simple: Was there a will? What is the estate worth once you set aside the homestead and exempt property? Are there debts beyond the mortgage? Does anyone need court authority to deal with a bank or title company? And how long ago did the person die — Texas generally requires a will to be offered for probate within four years.

The answers sort most El Paso families into one of three paths: a small estate affidavit for a modest estate with no will, a muniment of title for a will and a clean estate, or an independent administration when someone needs to be formally in charge. A fourth, a determination of heirship, applies when there is no will and the estate is too large for an affidavit. This page is general information, not legal advice about your family's estate. Se habla español.

sections.heading: Small Estate Affidavit Under Estates Code Chapter 205
paragraphs: The small estate affidavit is the fastest and least expensive way to collect a modest estate, and it is available only when the person died without a will. The requirements: at least 30 days have passed since death, no one has applied to be appointed personal representative, the estate's assets (not counting the homestead and other exempt property such as a vehicle and household furnishings) are worth no more than $75,000, and those assets exceed the known debts other than debts secured by exempt property. Typical examples are a bank account, a final paycheck, a small retirement balance, and the house the surviving spouse lived in.

The affidavit lists every asset, every debt, and every heir with their share under the intestacy rules, sworn to by all the heirs and by two disinterested witnesses who knew the family. The probate court approves it, and a certified copy is presented to the bank, the county clerk or the Texas DMV to transfer the asset. One limit matters: a small estate affidavit can transfer the homestead only to a surviving spouse or minor children. We prepare the affidavit, collect the signatures in one sitting at our conference table, and file it; most are approved within a few weeks.

sections.heading: Muniment of Title When There Is a Will
paragraphs: If your parent or spouse left a valid will and the estate owes nothing beyond a mortgage or other debt secured by real estate, Chapter 257 lets the court admit the will to probate as a muniment of title — old legal vocabulary meaning simply "evidence of ownership." No executor is appointed, no letters testamentary issue, and no inventory is filed. The court's order, with the will attached, becomes the document that transfers the house, land or vehicles to the people named in the will.

The hearing is short. We file the application with the original will and a death certificate, the clerk posts notice, and the judge hears brief testimony that the will is valid and the estate qualifies. If the will has a self-proving affidavit, no witnesses are needed. Filing to signed order is typically a month or two in El Paso. A muniment works well for a house and vehicles; it works poorly when a bank insists on letters testamentary, in which case an independent administration is the better choice from the start.

sections.heading: Independent Administration in the El Paso County Probate Courts
paragraphs: When someone needs real authority — to sell a house, settle with creditors, collect a retirement account, or deal with heirs who disagree — the court appoints a personal representative. Texas's independent administration under Chapter 401 makes this manageable: once appointed, the executor or administrator acts without asking the court's permission for each step. Most lawyer-drafted wills request it; where there is no will, all the heirs can agree to it.

El Paso County's probate matters are heard at the courthouse downtown. The process runs: application filed, notice posted by the clerk, a short hearing where the applicant testifies and takes the oath, letters issued, notice to creditors published, and an inventory filed within 90 days. An uncontested administration is usually opened within four to eight weeks.

One rule surprises families: because an executor or administrator acts on behalf of the heirs and creditors, not just themselves, Texas courts generally require that the representative be represented by a licensed attorney. A family member cannot open an administration pro se.

sections.heading: Transferring the House, the Vehicle and the Accounts
paragraphs: The reason to probate is usually one specific asset. For a house, the county clerk needs a recorded instrument showing the chain of ownership: the certified muniment order or small estate affidavit, or a deed signed by the independent executor. Until then the heirs cannot sell, refinance or insure it in their own names. For a vehicle, the Texas DMV accepts a certified probate order or, for small estates, an heirship affidavit on its own form. For bank accounts without a payable-on-death beneficiary, the bank wants letters testamentary or an approved small estate affidavit. Assets with a named beneficiary, survivorship accounts and property under a transfer-on-death deed bypass probate entirely, and part of the consultation is sorting what needs court action from what does not.

Fees are flat and quoted after a free consultation for uncontested matters, with court costs disclosed separately. If the death also left open tickets or warrants in the decedent's name, we can close those out too. And if this makes you realize your own documents are missing, our will and power of attorney packages are a short appointment away. Contact us to begin.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to probate an estate in El Paso?
faqs.a: For an independent administration, yes — Texas courts generally require the executor or administrator to be represented by an attorney because they act for other people. For a small estate affidavit or a muniment of title the court does not strictly require one, but the filings are easy to get wrong.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for a small estate affidavit in Texas?
faqs.a: An estate with no will, worth $75,000 or less excluding the homestead and exempt property, where 30 days have passed since death and no administration is pending. All heirs and two disinterested witnesses must sign.

faqs.q: What is a muniment of title?
faqs.a: A Texas procedure under Estates Code Chapter 257 that admits a will to probate as proof of ownership without appointing an executor. It is available when the estate has no unpaid debts other than those secured by real estate and no other need for administration.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in El Paso County?
faqs.a: A small estate affidavit is often approved within a few weeks. A muniment of title typically takes a month or two. An uncontested independent administration is usually opened within four to eight weeks and closed once assets are collected and creditors handled, commonly six months to a year.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline to probate a will in Texas?
faqs.a: Generally a will must be offered for probate within four years of death. After that, it can usually only be admitted as a muniment of title, and only if the applicant was not at fault for the delay. If a parent died years ago and the house is still in their name, there is often still a path.

faqs.q: My parent died with no will and the house is in their name. What do we do?
faqs.a: If the estate is small and the house is going to a surviving spouse or minor children, a small estate affidavit may work. If adult children are inheriting, the usual route is a determination of heirship, sometimes combined with an independent administration.
